messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: inits
parts:
In Rstan it would be helpful to be able to specify inits for just a subset of parameters. Something came up today, I added a strong prior to a parameter and then Stan got completely stuck, I think because it was having trouble getting from the starting values to the main area of the posterior distributions. So it seemed that specifying inits would help. But this was a pain in the ass because I then need (I think) to specify inits for all the parameters in the model. It would be helpful to be able to give inits for just one parameter or just a subset of parameters, with the understanding that automatic inits would be used for those parameters not specified.
Does this make sense?
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] inits
parts:
Yes, and it's already in the works. Jiqiang did an implementation
for RStan, but Daniel wants to reimplement. But Daniel's bogged
down by about a dozen other higher priorities, so no idea when it
could happen.

So you (Andrew) might want to push back on this if you need it
right away. I don't think we should hold up important features
just because we know there's a better way to implement them in
the future. As long as we get the interfaces fixed and the testing
done, swapping in new implementations should be easy.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] inits
parts:
On Friday, February 13, 2015 at 9:29:52 PM UTC-5, Andrew Gelman wrote:
No, I don’t need it right away.  It doesn’t kill me to just specify all the inits manually.  No rush.

One trick is to do 1 iteration with default inits, grab those with

inits <- get_inits(stanfit)

replace the inits you don't like, and call stan() with inits = inits.

Ben
